chunk_map.heading: ## Phase 1: Read what the failed run did
## Pin each failure to a quoted moment
## Phase 2: Match each failure to the check that catches it
## Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure
## Phase 4: Write the reference and plan.md
## Check both files are for the agent, not you

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Swept all nine chunks against the expanded body and the prior-slide history. The revised chunk 3 transition resolves in order: 'full three-way mapping' is the response to that slide's prompt; 'other two pieces' resolves to the verifier/reference/plan triad named in chunk 0; 'the rest' means the two non-dominant mappings; Phase 3 and Phase 4 are real later headers. Chunk 6's stop gate resolves entirely in-slide: 'the prompt' is immediately above it, 'that' is the prompt's continued looking, the five threshold nouns are the artefact criteria just specified, 'the second session' was named as the packaged re-send in chunk 0, and 'until then' points to saying 'lock it in.' Session-artifact and arc-earned-vocabulary carve-outs cover the run, transcript, branch, worktree, rules, and module names. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent remains.

No claim depends on an ambiguous file position. Chunk 0's worktree setup, Debrief re-send, and closing-lecture promise are module-arc/navigation beats and were verified against the host module's setup, re-send, and named closing lectures. Chunk 2's Module 1 callback identifies both the module and the repo-read claim, then restates the working prior in the same sentence. Chunk 8 names M1, optional M3, and M6 by stable module identifiers and exact artefacts/actions rather than by 'earlier' or 'next' position. No positional callback harm is present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Resolved the shared exercise through site/layouts/curriculum.js to AE101 M5 learn-from-the-test.md and checked its current include order. The worktree setup exists before the exercise (module lines 38-62); the exercise is included at line 64; the Debrief/re-send and fresh M5 long-run exist after it (module lines 74-102 plus trainer runtime); and the two closing lectures are included at lines 104-106. what-packaging-is.md explicitly names the three pieces the student assembled. Chunk 8's M6 stale-rule promise resolves to the current M6 module. No dead beat remains.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal or predict-before-outcome construction appears in the body; the prompts ask the agent to diagnose, map, build, and test rather than asking the student to guess an unrevealed result.

Every chunk carries an actionable claim. The thinnest slides still self-carry: chunk 2 turns generalised diagnosis into quoted evidence; chunk 5 states and executes the verifier smoke-test; chunk 7 distinguishes agent-consumable artefacts from generic advice; chunk 8 supplies the lock-in action, recap, and hand-off. None is a bare wait-state.

All eight H2 headers are literally true summaries of their chunks. In particular, chunk 3 does match each failure to a check and then narrows the student's decision; chunk 6 authors the reference and plan.md in conversation while reserving disk persistence for the later Approve slide, which is consistent with 'Write' as the phase-level activity; chunk 7 checks both artefacts; chunk 8 locks them in. No header contradicts its slide.

Checked all six sub-items in every chunk outside the recorded fence ranges: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction, no empty third anaphora/epistrophe leg, no self-grading superlative, no number followed by its own retraction, no abstraction-noun stack, and no empty-leg verb triplet. Chunk 2's 'about 10%' is a single working prior, not a retracted number, and its maintainer accept-note explicitly preserves that shape. The revised Phase 2 transition is four plain declaratives, not LLM cadence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No compendium, surface-as-noun, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun, or authorial 'beat' language appears in the body. 'Fire'/'fires' describes when a verifier, hook, or failure condition triggers; for AE101 engineer ICs this is ordinary technical event language, not repo-maintainer dialect. 'Teaching moment' is plain classroom prose, not the repository's specialised 'beat' vocabulary. The internal-dialect harm—forcing the room to decode author tooling language—is absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The maintainer block explicitly limits bold to title-page labels/widget chrome, the three verifier-shape menu handles, and the Phase 4 stop-gate handle. Chunk 6 has one bold element: 'Cut the grill when the package is good enough to re-send.' It is longer than the usual short handle, but functions as the slide's single governor and makes the cognitive-load escape valve visible at the exact point of use; the rest of the callout is plain. The proxy (a sentence-length bold span) fires, but the harm this rule prevents—bold monoculture and loss of visual hierarchy—is not present, and de-emphasising the stop gate would make the artefact worse. The revised Phase 2 transition has zero bold. No slide carries narrative-lead bolding or per-bullet emphasis monoculture.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The AE101 M5 host includes this file as an Exercise at learn-from-the-test.md line 64. The build's exercise inclusion path wraps it as a phase--exercise unit consumed by buildDeckModel; all body chunks sit inside that exercise and therefore reach the composed Slides deck. No phase-less prose in this file is dropped from the default view.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The content-ordinal headers are consecutive Phase 1 through Phase 4; the four intervening action headers are correctly unnumbered. Body references to Phase 3, Phase 4, and 'before Phase 4' resolve to real later headers in this file. scripts/check-slide-numbering.js completed cleanly across 59 files, including this target. No hand-numbered slide position or unresolved content ordinal appears.
